description.gco:CharacterString: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 03/31/2022 In September 1995, the GLBA hand-drawn mylar Land Resources Division segment sheets were created. They were continually revised as needed until 2003. In 1996, the park boundary and tracts were digitized from the Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve segment maps by NPS-contractor GeoNorth Inc. using ESRI software in the form of coverages, and, under the direction of the GIS and Lands Teams. Other digital sources used in the initial digital data set included: best available hydrography and digital public lands survey system maps. In 1997, all disposed tracts outside of the park boundary were dropped from the GIS. From 1999 to 2001, Encompass Mapping and Data, under contract to NPS and using ESRI software in the form of coverages, began a major update and revision process of the park boundary and tracts. Attribute and linework errors were resolved, better digital sources were used (DOQQs, survey data, revised USGS hydrography, PLSS, etc.), and land status changes were updated. From 2002 to 2009, many boundary and tract changes were either performed by the cartographer for the Alaska Land Resources Program Center using either Autodesk or ArcGIS software, then submitted in the form of Autodesk-exported or native ArcGIS shapefiles, jpegs, and requested attribute changes to Encompass Mapping and Data; or, the data was created/edited by Encompass Mapping and Data under the direction of the Lands cartographer. Most of the changes made by the Lands cartographer consisted of moving tracts to more accurate locations, cogoing the U.S., M.S., BLM, and NPS surveys using survey and Autodesk software, using the written legal descriptions for the park boundaries, using private and federal deed descriptions/plats, NOAA-surveyed shorelines, and using better orthophoto/DRG data to digitize shorelines, ridge boundaries, etc. In 2006, a new tract was created to show the new City of Gustavus boundary line now inside the park. A small northern portion of GLBA marine shoreline was revised in 2007 using accurate 2001 NOAA Mean High Water linework created from hydrographic survey techniques. The bulk of the shoreline for GLBA, however, was digitized by GLBA personnel using photography acquired in the approx. early 2000's. It mostly follows the edge of vegetation (generally higher than the Mean High Water mark). In 2007-8, the Falls Creek Exchange was completed (surveyed by BLM in 2004) which reduced a portion of the park (to State of Alaska) east of Gustavus and increased wilderness acreage for Cenotaph Island and an unnamed island near Blue Mouse Cove. The shoreline near Icy Bay and Dry Bay was digitized in 2008 by the Lands Cartographer using early 2000's satellite imagery. Encompass converted the data into ArcInfo files, attributed it, and submitted the data each time to the GIS team for inclusion into the GIS Permanent Data Set (PDS). NPS administrative parcels outside of the park were mapped by Lands during 2007-2008. In 2008, the Cobell restrictions on gov't. use of Native Allotment data were lifted so all Native Allotment data were returned to the GIS/Lands geodatabase. During 2009+, the common boundary with the U.S. Forest Service Tongass National Forest and the GLBA boundary is undergoing a process to edit and create one common boundary line along the ridges, rivers, and coast. This is being accomplished by Alaska Lands and GIS cartographers/GIS specialists from both agencies. In April 2009, Encompass Mapping and Data converted all lands data from coverages into a land status and boundary geodatabase created under contract to the AKRO-GIS Team. Specifications as delineated by GIS and Lands personnel were followed. In progress 2009, many of the native allotments are being cogoed-in by Lands Cartographers. 2008+, BLM-produced digital cogoed native allotments and other U.S. Surveys are also being incorporated into the NPS lands system after comparing to NPS cogo work or other maps. In the summer of 2009, the BLM will resurvey a portion of the park boundary which surrounds the City of Gustavus. Tract and boundary data is continually updated with land status changes and ongoing improvement of linework/attribution as better source information becomes available. The tract and boundary data has all been reprojected (when needed) to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude and longitude. A major remapping effort was completed for ~90% of the native allotments and other small private parcels. They were systematically revised and/or checked for correct location and conveyance status. Most were remapped by COGOing in US Survey plats and/or legal descriptions or using BLM-COGOed data. Previous to these edits, most small tracts were digitized from the hard copy Segment Sheets.In addition, satellite and aerial photo ortho imagery were used to move the tracts to better locations when the latitude/longitude of the parcels were too approximate or unknown. New tracts have been broken out of existing tracts where a subdivision and sale has been made to a non-native person(s). Continuous minor editing has been performed on park boundaries where better orthoimagery and/or common boundary agreements with adjoining federal agencies have been agreed upon per the "Alaska Common Boundary Initiative". No acreage changes are taking place. Native corporation conveyance actions have been updated as the changes take place. This involves deleting selections in some cases to changing from selected status into conveyed status. Survey plats and notes are always used to COGO in the boundaries. All tracts outside the park boundaries have now been mapped.

description.gco:CharacterString: Glen Canyon National Recreation Area Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 10/24/2018 Information contained in LRD's land ownership databases is updated nightly however tract polygons are posted to the NPS Data Store on a monthly basis. Users can ensure parcel polygons have up to date ownership attribution after the publication date by contacting your regional LRD office or downloading the Current_Tract_Ownership_Data file located on the NPS Data Store (http://science.nature.nps.gov/nrdata/) in a dBase format. Please contact the data originator with any suggested corrections and updates. LRD's boundary polygons represent the current legislated boundary of a given NPS unit. NPS does not necessarily have full fee ownership or hold another interest (easement, right of way, etc...) in all parcels contained within this boundary. Equivalently NPS may own or have an interest in parcels outside the legislated boundary of a given unit. In order to obtain complete information about current NPS interests both inside and outside the units legislated boundary, LRD's tracts files should also be downloaded and used in conjunction with LRD's boundary files. Process BLM GCDB files by creating the DXF file, assigning an appropriate coordinate system (UTM NAD 83 datum, Zone 12, US Foot; Central Meridian 111dW) for each GCDB file, attaching the GCDB file to the Glen Canyon drawing, and moving the imported layers to their appropriate layers (PLSS-Township, PLSS Section, and PLSS Subdivin). Downloaded 5 hypsography files from NPS data store for Glen Canyon Hypsography. Copied tract boundaries line work for tracts and moved them to the “tract” layer. Created text links for tract boundaries. Created and Exported 8 shapefiles of the 3720 contour line for Glen Canyon. COGO’d boundary lines for the tracts, lots, and blocks within the Page Subdivision (Glen Canyon) using BLM surveys. Created Shapefile to transform and georeference the tracts, lots, and blocks for Page Subdivision. Input 8 Northing and Eastings into excel file, added the excel sheet to ArcMap, converted to a dbf file, added the XY data, and exported shapefile. Transformed and rotated tracts, lots, and blocks for Page Subdivision to the Georeferenced shapefile created in ArcMap. Labeled 794 Parcels within the Page Subdivision. Digitized right and left bank of the Colorado River from the Glen Canyon Dam to the south border of the Exported San Juan, and Colorado River center line and shoreline (submerged stream) polygons from ArcMap. Imported the shapefiles into Autodesk. For GLCA Segment Maps 2, 3,5,6: copied the submerged stream and Colorado River centerline line work into the Tract layer. Islands within the river were copied to the Tract-Sec Layer. Cleaned up line work for the various segments. Created tract 03-115 in Segment 3 of GLCA since I now have the Colorado River Bank information. Created the text link for the tract as well. Cleaned Up line work for segments 1-10 in GLCA. This included going through each segment and carefully looking at the PLSS sections, subdivision, and township layer to make sure that all miniscule lines were on the correct layer. This also included going through each township label to make sure it was correct and all labels were uniform in position. Carefully reviewed all 794 parcels within the Page subdivision of GLCA to make sure all labels were placed accurately and uniform. Created a 24k topo mosaic for the entire GLCA park. 62 Tiles total. On screen digitized the 3720’ Contour line from the 24k topo mosaic created for GLCA. The southern boundary line for GLCA was digitized in the following areas: t42.5S-r8e, t43s-8e,t42s-r9e, t42s-r11e, t41s-r12e, t41s-r10e, t42s-r9e, t40s-r11e, t41s-r13e, t40s-r14e, t40s-e15e, t40s-16e. Digitized the Eastern bank of the river in t40s-r7e. Drew in the .05 Rivermile Marker as well as the 72.7 Rivermile Marker in segment maps 7 and 9. This was done by adding up the San Juan River segments until they measured 72.7 miles in length from where the San Juan River and Colorado River Confluence is. The .05 Rivermile marker was done the same way except the Colorado River Line Segments were added up until they measured .05 miles in length from the Boat Launch pad in SW 1/4, Section 18, T40S, R8E. On Screen Digitized Northwest boundary of Lot 7, Block 18, in the Page Subdivision for GLCA On screen digitized the boundary for Block 16 in the Page subdivision. Did so by using a 44 foot offset from the centerline of road. COGO’d the boundary for tracts 241003-103, 241003-105, 241003106, 241003-107 in T34s-R13e, section 35. Inserted text link as well. Created tracts 241009-101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107. This included copying line work and moving it to the tracts layer, then adding the text link. Created and Exported tract and boundary topology for GLCA. UPDATE: 04/17/2014 GRCA boundary sections that are defined as the “high-water mark” of the Colorado River were delineated by digitizing from two primary data sources: 1) High-resolution (18-cm) color-infrared imagery from the USGS GCMRC (Grand Canyon Monitoring and Research Center; 2002, 2005 and 2009), and 2) modeled flow lines from the US Bureau of Reclamation (BOR, Wright, et al., 2004), based on 1-meter LIDAR. Both primary sources were supplemented by an ISTAR 2002 Digital Surface Model (DSM), alternate high-resolution imagery, USGS GCMRC modeled flow lines (Magirl, et al., 2008), and on-the-ground mapping. Where using high-resolution imagery, the high-water mark is clearly visible thorough changes in vegetation, soil, bedrock bleaching, etc. This method was used in the Lee’s Ferry area (GCMRC River Mile 0-1.1, river right), near Parashant Canyon (RM 198.2-201.4, river left), and downstream of Diamond Creek to Lake Mead (RM 226.2-273.9, river left). The BOR flow lines were primarily used upstream from Navajo Bridge (RM 0-4.54, river left; RM 1.1-4.56, river right), between Tuckup and Parashant Canyons (RM 165.2-198.2, river left), and fom below Tuckup Canyon (RM 201.4) to below Diamond Creek Rapids (RM 226.2). The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.

description.gco:CharacterString: Golden Gate National Recreation Area Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 03/24/2026 Added GOGA 05-171 tract based on PORE 15-127. 2023 Marin County parcel data was used. Minor boundary adjustment still required. Updated tract 20-125. Previous boundary included private property. 2022 San Mateo County parcels were used for consistency. GOGA Legislative boundary was shifted to match tract. Tract 23-104 and tract 20-137 (Mori Point) were modified based on 2019 record of survey. Minor change to GOGA Legislative boundary. Added GOGA tract 23-120. Minor boundary adjustment still required. Used 2022 San Mateo County parcel data. Will update this tract and the adjacent tracts 23-118 and 23-119 if a survey or better data becomes available. UPDATE: 03/17/2024 Tract 01-122 was created from Tract 01-120. This tract existed in previous GOGA boundary datasets and segment maps. It must have been accidentally deleted. The polygon was created using the 1970 Tronoff survey to the north and the 1975 BLM survey (GOGA BLM 5) survey to the south. UPDATE: 03/15/2024 Complete update to Segments 02, 03, 04 & 05 (Marin County). Known boundary issues in these segments, mainly conflicts between local surveys and the 1976 BLM survey and several known encroachments, prompted in-depth land records research. Private survey plats filed in Marin County were cross-checked with federal land record information. Areas of conflict are identified with new tracts for further research. GPS point data for survey monuments in these segments was utilized to anchor survey traverse data. The tract boundaries adjoining Bolinas Bay were updated to reflect current MHW as represented utilizing current aerial photography. These boundaries are riparian in nature and are therefore subject to the continual natural movement of the tides. UPDATE: 05/01/2015 The accuracy of the data varies depending upon source data used in various areas of the park. The order in which the segments are referenced this metadata are in the order that they were completed. They were completed in a particular order due to a request from the Golden Gate GIS specialist. For segment 01, the majority of the boundary was COGOd using BLM ROS 5 and tied down to the ground with GPS points provided by the GIS specialist from GOGA. The shoreline was created by using NOAA shoreline data, and consequently the 50 year lease tracts were created by performing a buffer off of the NOAA shoreline. The remainder of the tracts were COGO'd through the use of legal descriptions, and/or deeds. FOPO and SAFR were COGO'd by a previous cartographer, but were repositioned to be tied down to BLM ROS 5. The "ALCATRAZ LIGHTHOUSE" was rotated around point (X = 6006552.64, Y = 2129010.40) to account for the ground to grid translation. Segment 24: Most of the areas on segment 24 were COGO'd by a previous cartographer with the Land Resources Divsion. All notes for transformations are as follows: Survey goga_bnd_t2_3n-r8w was transformed around U.S.C. & G.S. "PACHECO" ( X = 5917751.75, Y = 2229089.44) and AP No. 23 (X = 5928671.75, Y = 2206271.21) to account for the ground to grid translation. Survey GOGA_641-41943 (AP no. 1 - AP No. 23) was transformed around U.S.C. & G.S. "FRANCIS" (X = 5999043.16, Y = 2122211.80) and Survey GOGA_641-41945 (AP no. 23- AP No. 194) was transformed around AP No. 30 (X = 5999266.64, Y = 2116745.92) and AP No. 192 (X = 5983656.46, Y = 2087799.29) to account for the ground to grid translation. Surveys GOGA_641-41941, GOGA_641-41937 and the east side of GOGA_641-41938 were transformed around Baker 2 (X = 5986922.81, Y = 2133471.54) and East Peak (X = 5962473.02, Y = 2167452.69) to account for the ground to grid translation. Survey goga_admin_bnd_t1s-r6w was transformed around U.S.C. & G.S. "MOUNT DIABLO 3" (X = 5983946.42, Y = 2127434.76) and "RANGE RESET" (X = 5992071.61, Y = 2132529.94) to account for the ground to grid translation. Survey GOGA_641-41939 rotated -1d20m43.825s and scaled by 0.999934273 around "Wilkens" ( X = 5927902.29, Y = 2170093.13) to account for the ground to grid translation. Survey 641-41938, only that portion which surrounds Rodeo Beach, was transformed around "ROOT" (X = 5940699.57, Y = 2158773.92) and LEON (X = 5944793.42, Y = 2158966.36) to account for the ground to grid translation. Survey t2s-r6w was transformed around "AP 154" (X = 5980684.59, Y = 2111355.50) and "AP 159" (X = 5980214.80, Y = 2111628.06) to account for the ground to grid translation. Survey t2s-r6w-block-1591 was transformed around "AP 153" (X = 5980994.95, Y = 2111348.41) and "AP 159" (X = 5980214.80, Y = 2111628.06) to account for the ground to grid translation. Tract 02-104 & 02-105 were transformed between station "STUART" (X = 5999979.90, Y = 2141796.45) and "LEDYARD" ( X = 6001283.12, Y = 2140123.71) to account for ground to grid translation. USGS DLG line work for mean high water line of Angel & Alcatraz Islands were used to define boundary. Tract 02-148 & 02-149 were transformed between station "BLUNT" (X = 6007642.05, Y = 2138838.73) and "LEDYARD" ( X = 6001283.12, Y = 2140123.71) to account for ground to grid translation. The remainder of the tracts were COGO'd from either deeds, legal descriptions or records of surveys and were tied down to existing linework. Much of segment 24 and 23 have overlapping tracts between segments. There are tracts along and including Sweeney Ridge that were tied to "FLAT" monument which was GPS'd by GOGA staff in the field. From the southeast corner of tract 20-111 to the northwest corner of tract 20-108 were cogo'd from BLM ROS, and tied down to Sweeney Ridge survey, and survey monuments. The interior tracts of 23-114, 23-113, 23-112, 23-111, 23-110, 23-109, and 23-108 were created using San Mateo County Parcel data due to lack of deeds, or legal descriptions in the area. Segment 22 was considerably difficult due to lack of monumentation, as well as surveys, deeds, and legal descriptions. This is likely the dataset's weakest area due to lack of data. San Mateo parcel data was used for tract 21-101 to depict the watershed district tract. Tracts 22-101, 22-102, and 22-103 were cogo'd from the BLM records of survey (ROS) 15-LLS-PG028, 13-LLS-PG109, and. 13-LLS-PG108. There is considerable overlap for segment 21 and segment 24. Many of the tracts were COGO'd by a previous cartographer, and his notes are located above. Tracts in the area were tied to existing tracts, except for tract 21-101, which as mentioned before, was created using San Mateo Parcel data due to lack over data for the area. As data becomes available for weak areas, they will be included in subsequent updates. For Segment 20, as mentioned before, Sweeney Ridge was COGO'd from BLM surveys, and tied down to the "FLAT" monument. From the southern point of tract 20-111 to the northwest point of tract 20-108, a BLM ROS was used to create the boundary which was then tied into the Sweeney Ridge Survey. GPS points from the park were also used to tie the data to the ground at the northwest corner of tract 20-108 as well as the southernmost portion of Sweeney Ridge, as well as the "FLAT" monument. Again, the remainder of tract 21-101 was created by using San Mateo County parcel data due to lack of surveys and legal descriptions in the area. Milagre Ridge was COGO'd through the use of BLM ROS, and was tied to the ground using GPS points provided by the park. GPS points were provided for all the main corners of tracts 20-107, 20-126, and 20-131, as well as the doughnuts within tract 20-107. The tracts were all transformed around point X = 59990877.840, Y = 205954.993. Much of the linework for Segments 02, 03, 07, 08, 04, and 05 were COGO'd through the us of the following BLM surveys : BLM 04, BLM 09, BLM 10, BLM 13, and BLM 14. Tracts on Segments 02, 03, 07, and 08 that were not included in those surveys, deeds, or legal descriptions were COGO'd from the Marin County legal descriptions/surveys that can be downloaded here by searching for a parcel number or map book and map page: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/ar/divisions/assessor/search-assessor-records. Tracts 02-196, 02-101-, 02-192 were on-screen digitized due to the lack of deeds, surveys, legal descriptions and parcel data. Segments 04, 05, and 09-19 are managed by PORE. The tracts within these segments were COGO'd through the us of surveys found from the Marin County assessors website here: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/ar/divisions/assessor/search-assessor-records. These tracts were tied down to known points, and linework such as MUWO boundary, as well as tracts from segments 02, and 03. As new data for Segments 04, 05, and 09-19 becomes available, they will be included in the GOGA dataset and re-released. Any tract without a deed, legal description, or survey within Segments 09-19 were created through the use of Marin County parcel data. Once the tracts and boundary for GOGA were drawin, they were copied to either the tract layer or boundary layer. The linework then underwent the topology building process, and was then exported to an ESRI ESRI Feature Class. The Horizonatal Accuracy of the San Francisco Parcel data is as follows: Global Positioning System (GPS) Control Survey: a GPS survey of 65 survey control points was conducted, generating coordinate and elevation data for the survey point network used for Basemap development. The network meets the National Geodetic Survey standard for Second Order, Class 2. Orthophoto accuracy: Ninety percent of points on an orthophoto are plus or minus 2.5 feet of survey point coordinates for the same point. Planimetric features (citylots, sfblocks, cityfeatures, street centerline files) are overlaid on the orthophoto images with an accuracy of plus or minus 2 foot. The horizontal accuracy of the Marin County Parcel data is as follows: Parcel boundaries were digitized from hard copy Assessor map pages into AutoCAD. Georeferencing was based on 400 scale mylar aerial photographs from 1976. Many Assessor map pages did not fit well together. In order to create a seamless layer, problem areas were stretched or compressed. Topology was created in AutoCAD and closed polygons were exported as an ESRI ESRI Feature Class. This ESRI Feature Class was imported into SDE to create the Parcel feature class. No Horizontal position accuracy was given for the San Mateo County parcels. The horizontal accuracy of the NOAA shoreline data is as follows: The shoreline and associated data are a representation based on an office interpretation of imagery and/or fieldwork at the time of survey. The attribute accuracy was tested by creating checkplots of the coded linework. The codes depict shoreline and several alongshore features. A light table review of the checkplots revealed any inaccurate coding. Mistakes were identified and corrected. These attributes were translated into NGS's Coastal Cartographic Object Attribute Source Table (C-COAST) for data consistency. The C-COAST attributes were given symbology and visually inspected to verify attribute accuracy. The horizontal accuracy of the DOQQ imagery should be considered no better than the following: USDA-FSA Aerial Photography Field Office relies on the integrity of the original data collection which was performed by private contractors. Data integrity was validated by the responsible private contractor or sub-contractor. Polygon and chain-node topology present. There are no duplicate arcs and no dangling nodes. The data set contains polygons that do not overlap, there are no polygons that are entered twice, and all areas are completely described. The area features are topologically structured with nodes at all intersections. Attribution of the digital data set includes polygon areas that define the portion of visible imagery used representing the same source acquisition date, with no gaps in coverage. This data set contains imagery from the National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP). The NAIP acquires digital ortho imagery during the agricultural growing seasons in the continental U.S.. A primary goal of the NAIP program is to enable availability of ortho imagery within one year of acquisition. The NAIP provides two main products: 1 meter ground sample distance (GSD) ortho imagery rectified to a horizontal accuracy within +/- 5 meters of reference digital ortho quarter quads (DOQQ's) from the National Digital Ortho Program (NDOP) or from the National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP); 1 meter GSD ortho imagery rectified within +/- 6 meters to true ground. The tiling format of NAIP imagery is based on a 3.75' x 3.75' quarter quadrangle with a 300 meter buffer on all four sides. The NAIP imagery is formatted to the UTM coordinate system using the North American Datum of 1983 (NAD83). The NAIP imagery may contain as much as 10% cloud cover per tile. This file was generated by compressing NAIP imagery that cover the county extent. Two types of compression may be used for NAIP imagery: MrSID and JPEG 2000. Target value for the compression ratio is (15:1). Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. As previously mentioned, GOGA is in a status of continual update, and as newer/better data becomes available, it will be included in the GOGA tract and boundary dataset. The native coordinate system for the DWG is California State Plane, Zone III, NAD83, US Foot. The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.

description.gco:CharacterString: Governors Island National Monument Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 03/24/2011 Tracts 01-101, 01-102, 01-103, 01-104, 01-105, and 01-106 were all input using "Exterior Boundary Survey of Tracts 01-101, 01-102, 01-103 & 01-104 for the U.S. Department of the Interior, National Park Service, Governors Island National Monument, City of New York, New York County, State of New York," Project Number 89821009, dated September 19, 2002, by Michael A. description.gco:CharacterString: Grand Canyon National Park Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 01/08/2021 Adjusted the legislated boundary to include tract 109-01. UPDATE: 07/16/2018 The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step. BLM GCDB data was used in order to complete the majority of the boundary and tracts for GRCA. This was done by importing GCDB files for each township and range that encompass the park. Where no GCDB data existed for Canyon Rim portions of the boundary, USGS SDTS hypsography files were processed in ArcMap and converted to converages, then converted to shapefiles. The boundary along the southern bank of the Colorado River was completed the same way by using USGS hydrography data. Where GCDB data did exist that coincided with the boundary, linework was copied from the PLSS layer to the tract or boundary layer. In order to map the interior and exterior tracts, deeds, legal descriptions, USGS SDTS transportation data, Arizona State Land Department, Arizona Land Resources Information System data was used. Some tract boundaries were not as definitive. The process for mapping these tracts is as follows: On-screen digitized east bank of Colorado river in T30N-R14W, SECTION 10 (NW1/4, NW1/4), Section 3 (SW ¼, SW1/4). Due to incomplete hydro data. On-screen digitized east bank of Colorado river in T31N-R14W, SECTION 29 (NW1/4, SW1/4 AND NW1/4, SE1/4), Section 30 (NE1/4, SE1/4 AND NE1/4, SW1/4 AND NW1/4, SW1/4 AND NW1/4, SE1/4 ). Due to incomplete hydro data. On-screen digitized east bank of Colorado river in T31N-R15W, SECTION 26 (NE1/4, NE1/4 AND NE1/4, NW1/4) Due to incomplete hydro data. Approximately 4066 feet north of the corner of T40N R7E DIGITIZED THE EAST RIM OF THE CANYON due to lack of hypsography for the Lee’s Ferry quadrangle. Mojave parcels imported, and transformed around points X = 1020605.23 Y = 13158684.38 and X = 1019313.87, Y = 13160032.84 Eastern boundary of tract 105-01 digitized from segment map. Tract 104-02 is 200ft right of way according to miscellaneous map grca11311976-001.pdf found here: http://landsnet.nps.gov/tractsnet/documents/grca/Miscellaneous_Maps/grca11311976-001.pdf. For further verification, the tract was accessed on the Coconino County Parcel Viewer, printed off to a scale of 1:600 (1:50ft) and then measured. Eastern boundary of tract 107-22 digitized from segment map. The Arizona state land ownership portion of the land coverage is updated along with the surface parcels coverage. All changes to the surface parcels are performed by the CAD department. They are then given to the GIS department in a DXF file on a township by township basis. Through a series of AMLs and editing procedures, the changes in the DXF file are incorporated into the surface parcels and land coverages. Changes in federal agencies are done primarily through the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) using a customized AML based application of ArcInfo. BLM incorporates its changes as well as others such as the Forest Service, Bureau of Reclamation, Fish & Wildlife Service, National Park Service, etc. BLM and State of Arizona status is updated approximately every six months, other agencies are updated on an irregular basis. Data is obtained from both the Bureau of Land Management and Bureau of Indian Affairs on a somewhat regular basis and incorporated into the land coverage as necessary. DOQQs production procedures, instrumentation, hardware and software used in the collection of standard USGS DOQ's vary depending on systems used at the contract, cooperator or USGS production sites. The majority of DOQ datasets are acquired through government contract. The process step describes, in general, the process used in the production of USGS DOQ data sets. The rectification process requires, as input, a user parameter file to the rectification process, a digital elevation model gridded to specified bounds, projection, zone, datum and X-Y units, a scanned image file covering the same area as the DEM, ground X-Y-Z point values and their conjugate photo coordinates in the camera coordinate system, and measurements of the fiducial in the digitized image. The camera calibration report provides the length of the camera and the distances in millimeters from the optical center to the camera's 8 fiducial marks. These marks define the field of reference for spatial measurements made from the photograph. Ground control points acquired from ground surveys or developed in aerotriangulation, are third order class 1 or better, and meet National Map Accuracy Standard (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale. Ground control points are in the Universal Transverse Mercator or the State Plane Coordinate System on NAD83. Horizontal and vertical residuals of aerotriangulated tie-points are equal to or less than 2.5 meters. Standard aerotriangulation passpoint configuration consists of 9 ground control points, one near each corner, one at the center near each side and 1 near the center of the photograph, are used. The conjugate positions of the ground control points on the photograph are measured and recorded in camera coordinates. The raster image file is created by scanning an aerial photograph film diapositive with a precision image scanner. An aperture of approximately 25 to 32 microns is used, with an aperture no greater than 32 microns permitted. Digital Line Graphs were digitized from the USGS source quadrangle, by either the National Mapping Division, one of their cooperators, or one of their contractors. The digital data were produced by one of the following methods: - scanning a stable-based copy of the graphic materials. The scanning process captured the digital data at a scanning resolution of at least 0.001 inches. Once tract and boundary data was complete, topology was successfully built and then exported. The data was georeferenced using UTM coordinate system, NAD 83, Zone 12. Once the shapefiles were exported, they were converted to LL83. USGS DLG 7.5’ Hypsography: USGS DLG Hypsography lines were traced to define the Grand Canyon Rim, beginning at well-defined clearly discernible rim locations from recognized reference data, including USGS 1:24K DRG topographic maps, USGS nominal 10-meter Digital Elevation Model data (derived slope model), USDA one-meter NAIP Imagery (2010 and 2007). Single Hypsographic lines were traced along the rim. At points where reference data visually indicate that the individual hypsographic contour line diverges from the canyon rim, tracing was offset to the next nearest hypsographic line that closest follows the canyon rim. In locations were the rim is not clearly shown on reference data, hypsographic contour lines from well-established locations were continued, where possible, so long as they generally followed GRCA Segment maps or other reference data. For side canyons, hypsographic rim contours were followed into side canyons, so long as they did not diverge significantly from GRCA Segment maps or other reference data. If this resulted in following a contour far beyond what was indicated on the Segment maps or other reference data, the digitized lines were stepped down/up along visible geographic features, in particular secondary side canyons or NHD Streamline features. Where GRCA Segment maps or Solicitor opinions indicate that the Boundary is offset from the canyon rim (this occurs on the South Rim, where the boundary is defined as “…one-quarter mile from the canyon rim…”), the defined canyon rim was buffered by the legislated distance. USGS DLG 7.5’ Boundary: Where reference data indicate that the GRCA Boundary does not follow the canyon rim, USGS DLG Boundary data were used wherever they have been defined. After careful inspection, this data is considered much truer to the Legislated Boundary than USBLM GCDB data of the same features. USGS NHD Area: USGS NHD Area data, downloaded in January 2011 from USGS, was used as the reference data where the GRCA Boundary is defined as the Colorado River bank. This occurs along the border with the Hualapai Reservation and along the GLCA Boundary. The data used is more recent than what had been previously used. USGS NHD Flowline: USGS NHD Flowline data was used where the GRCA Boundary is defined by a stream course. This occurs in only one location, along Indian Hollow and Jumpup Canyons. The original legislation defining the park boundary in T32N R15W references an “unsurveyed township” meaning the United States government had not completed a rectangular survey of the area being defined at the time of legislation. The congressional action assumed the sections would be surveyed in a “typical” manner, meaning 36 regular sections of approximately 640 acres each, one mile per section side. When the survey was completed, an irregular township (32½ N) was added to the north of T32N. The boundary identified in the legislation contains a call to section 25 (unsurveyed). The current location of section 25 is now south of the intended location by about 3,600 feet (due to the irregular township). Because the intended location of the legislated boundary is based on an assumed regular township, the boundary does not match the section calls in the legislation. Historical boundary maps of GRCA confirm this boundary location. Please reference map number 133/20,021-B for the legislated boundary. Any Navajo Lands within the boundary depicted on this map are a part of the legislated boundary, and may be different than the administrative boundary. Also, notes will appear on the Land Status Maps in these areas, in order to avert confusion with regards to any and all Navajo Lands that fall within the legislated boundary.

description.gco:CharacterString: Grand Teton National Park Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 03/13/2025 Tract 06-102 modified to account for full fee ownership after acquisition UPDATE: 12/04/2023 Edits made to tract 04-105 to merge tracts 04-105A and 04-105B. Tracts 04-105A and 04-105B were created solely to track exchange of land and have been archived. UPDATE: 09/12/2023 Tracts 04-105 and 04-145 were modified to create tracts 04-105A, 04-105B, and 04-145-1 which were involved in an exchange of land between NPS and the private landowner. Adjustments were made using the survey by Gary Grigsby, PE, PLS License No. 9283 dated 05/6/2022 (Filed at County on 1/9/2023, doc #1052447). UPDATE: 03/22/2022 PLSS for Teton county was downloaded from the BLM's state site (http://www.blm.gov/wy/st/en/resources/public_room/gis/datagis/county/gcdb.html) in coverage format on 20080602. The AutoCAD Map IMPORT command used to import these coverages. This information was used as a base to geo-reference the boundary and tracts for GRTE. Not all of GRTE has been surveyed, so projected sections were created (i.e, around Jackson Lake). Tracts that were described by aliquot part descriptions were created making copies of this line work. For those tracts described by bearing and distance descriptions, this PLSS layer was also used as points-of-beginning and a basis for ground to grid scale and rotation transformations. The horizontal accuracy of the surveyed townships for GRTE is NOT consistent. Therefore, the PLSS line work was not used in these cases. Used Watershed boundary ArcInfo coverage from the University of Wyoming's Geographic Information Science Center (http://www.wygisc.uwyo.edu/) to delineate hydrographic boundaries. This dataset meets federal standards for delineation of hydrologic unit boundaries. Local experts (Frank Jackson of the USFS and Paul Caffrey of UWyo) suggested that this boundary rather than the USGS National Hydrography Dataset (NHD) data because of their confidence in this dataset. It was downloaded on 20080409. This dataset defined the hydrographic boundaries for tracts 10-120 and 11-115. For those tracts that follow the centerline of a road (e.g., Moose-Wilson Road)or the bank or main thread of a watercourse (Snake and Gros Ventre Rivers), 2006 NAIP ortho-photography was on-screen digitized to create boundaries. Tracts 06-127 & 06-127A were entered using COGO from the description included with the grant of easement. The AutoCAD Project was projected to Wyoming State Plane, Zone West, NAD83, US Foot. The AutoCAD line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from AutoCAD to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.

description.gco:CharacterString: Guilford Courthouse National Military Park Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 09/23/2020 See Tony Marshall for update details. UPDATE: 06/17/2015 Guilford county parcel data was obtained for digital data conversion. The native projection for the parcel data was NAD 83. The tracts and boundary for GUCO were COGO'd from deeds, legal descriptions, and copied over from the Montgomery and Greene County parcel data. They were then copied to their appropriate layer; either the tract layer or boundary layer. The line work was laid over NAIP aerial imagery for the area as well. For the DOQQs the horizontal positional accuracy and the assurance of that accuracy depend, in part, on the accuracy of the data inputs to the rectification process. These inputs consist of the digital elevation model (DEM),aerotriangulation control and methods, the photo source camera calibration, scanner calibration, and aerial photographs that meet National Aerial Photography Program (NAPP) standards. The vertical accuracy of the verified USGS format DEM is equivalent to or better than a USGS level 1 or 2 DEM, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of no greater than 7.0 meters. Field control is acquired by third order class 1 or better survey methods sufficiently spaced to meet National Map Accuracy Staandards (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale products. Aerial cameras have current certification from the USGS, National Mapping Division, Optical Science Laboratory. Test calibration scans are performed on all source photography scanners. Horizontal positional accuracy is determined by the Orthophoto Accuracy (ORACC) software program for DOQ data produced by the National Mapping Division. The program determines the accuracy by finding the line and sample coordinates of the passpoints in the DOQ and fitting these to their ground coordinates to develop a root mean square error (RMSE). From 4 to 9 points are checked. As a further accuracy test, the image line and sample coordinates of the DEM corners are transformed and compared with the actual X,Y DEM corner values to determine if they are within the RMSE. For the BLM GCDB Data the majority of coordinates in this dataset fall within +/- 40 feet spatial accuracy (the general rule of thumb to be called 1:24,000-scale data). For the DOQQs the horizontal positional accuracy and the assurance of that accuracy depend, in part, on the accuracy of the data inputs to the rectification process. These inputs consist of the digital elevation model (DEM),aerotriangulation control and methods, the photo source camera calibration, scanner calibration, and aerial photographs that meet National Aerial Photography Program (NAPP) standards. The vertical accuracy of the verified USGS format DEM is equivalent to or better than a USGS level 1 or 2 DEM, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of no greater than 7.0 meters. Field control is acquired by third order class 1 or better survey methods sufficiently spaced to meet National Map Accuracy Staandards (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale products. Aerial cameras have current certification from the USGS, National Mapping Division, Optical Science Laboratory. Test calibration scans are performed on all source photography scanners. Horizontal positional accuracy is determined by the Orthophoto Accuracy (ORACC) software program for DOQ data produced by the National Mapping Division. The program determines the accuracy by finding the line and sample coordinates of the passpoints in the DOQ and fitting these to their ground coordinates to develop a root mean square error (RMSE). From 4 to 9 points are checked. As a further accuracy test, the image line and sample coordinates of the DEM corners are transformed and compared with the actual X,Y DEM corner values to determine if they are within the RMSE. Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. The Native coordinate system for the DWG is North Carolina State Plane, NAD83, US Foot. The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.

description.gco:CharacterString: Gulf Islands National Seashore Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 12/16/2024 Tract 05-150 - Road was identified as a 9 acre parcel alleged to be owned by the park. Tract 05-151 which is supposed to represent the disposal of 05-150. The park doesn’t own the tract 05-150. Changes are to reflect that. Tract 03-125 VFW Land exchange – (Jackson County, Mississippi). The boundary was redrawn by Congress for this small land exchange with the VFW in 2019. Geometry updated. UPDATE: 06/10/2010 Line work was digitized from the original Mylar Land Status Map of the Gulf Islands National Seashore in 2002, using AutoCAD Land Development Desktop (LDD) by Avineon, Inc., 4825 Mark Center Drive, Suite 700, Alexandria VA 22311-1846. POC: Xiaodong Hong, Manager, Geographic Information Systems, (703) 671-1900. Email: xhong@avineon.com. Digitized line work was then verified by the SER Office personnel from deeds, legal descriptions, and survey data (when available). Map Projection is Mississippi State Plane, East zone, NAD83, US foot . When discrepancies were identified, individual tracts were re-plotted by use of COGO, using AutoCAD LDD. Data was geo-referenced to DOQQ, Mississippi State Plane, East Zone, NAD 83. Topology was created for park boundary and individual tracts. Primary validation of cartographic attributes was verified by displaying the lines in both database and the spatial coverage, but no formal tests were performed. Database attributes were linked during the topology creation process. Database attributes were retrieved from the National Park Service, Management Information System, Master Deeds List (MIS/MDL). Clean Topology was developed and attributes were assigned in AutoCad Map using the Drawing Clean-up function at a tolerance level of 0.10 and Object Data links. Per deed guis34, tract 06-107 was drawn as "all of sections 33 and 34, Township 2 South, Range 29 West, and sections 2 and 3, Township 3 South, Range 29 West...less the portion thereof lying below the mean high tide (water) line." The most current PLSS linework was downloaded from Geocommunicator and was utilized for determining the boundary for this tract. The mean high water line for the Florida portion of the National Seashore was drawn per NOAA Nautical Chart 11382 dated May 29, 2010 and NOAA Nautical Chart 11388 dated February 2004. Tracts 06-105 and 06-106 were drawn by offsetting the north and south boundary of tract 06-107 300 feet as per deed guis08. Tract 05-137 was drawn from deed guis07 using cogo commands in Autodesk. Roadways detailed in deed guis07 as reference points were on-screen digitized based on 2006 NAIP 1m imagery. Tract 05-107 was drawn by on-screen digitizing the mean high water line from NOAA Nautical Chart 11382 dated May 29, 2010. This line was offset 300 feet per Legislative map GUIS_635_7100J. Tracts 05-108, 05-109, and 05-149 were on-screen digitized based on Land Status Segment Map 5 dated January 8, 1971 and were matched to tract 05-137 at point x=1468233.396, y=314545.674. The boundary line for Cat Island was drawn by on-screen digitizing the mean low water line from NOAA Nautical Chart 11372 (dated January 12, 2010). The resulting mean low water line was offset one mile (5,280 feet) per Legislative Map, numbered NS-GI-7100J dated December 1970 listed in P.L. 91-660, 84 Stat. 1967. Tracts 12-101 and 12-102 were drawn based on the on-screen digitization of the mean high water line from NOAA Nautical Chart 11372 (dated January 12, 2010) and from ground control point coordinates as shown on survey map 635/60021 last updated on March 26, 2002. Tract 12-108 is an easement over the dry land of the parcel of land known as the Boddie Family Tract. This tract was drawn by on screen digitizing the South Bayou Marsh as seen on NOAA Nautical Chart 11372 dated January 12, 2010 and a legal description found in P.L. 106-554, 114 Stat. 2763A-231 dated December 21, 2000. Ship Island, Horn Island, and Petit Bois Island: The boundary line for Ship Island, Horn Island, and Petit Bois Island was drawn by on-screen digitizing the mean low water line from NOAA Nautical Chart 11373 (dated November 10 2009). The resulting mean low water line was offset one mile (5,280 feet) per Legislative Map, numbered NS-GI-7100J dated December 1970 listed in P.L. 91-660, 84 Stat. 1967. Exterior boundaries for tracts 03-114, 03-115, 03-116, 03-117, 03-118, 03-121, 03-125, 03-127, 03-130, 03-134, and 03-135 were drawn using cogo commands in AutoDesk based on Boundary Survey Map 635-41,007B dated May 1982. All allequate part interior tract boundaries for these tracts were drawn using the most recent available PLSS linework and the appropriate deed. No deed or legal description was available for Tract 03-140, and so it was drawn per sm03 dated 1972. Tract 07-105 was on screen digitized from 2006 NAIP 1m imagery. Centerline was on-screen digitized and offset 40 feet. Tracts 01-103, 01-104, 01-105, 01-106, and 01-107 were drawn based on directions and distances from the latitude and longitude coordinates for the Ship Island Lighthouse located at latitude 30d12'.1" and longitude 88d57'.8""as detailed in their respective deeds. Tracts 01-101, 01-110, and the eastern boundary for tract 01-106 were drawn based on directions and distances from the latitude and longitude coordinates for the United States Coast and Geodetic Survey triangulation station located at latitude 30d13'.257"and Longitude 88d53'.884" as detailed in their respective deeds. Boundaries following shipping channels were on-screen digitized from NOAA Nautical Chart 11373 (dated November 10, 2009). Additional surveys, legal descriptions, change orders, and deeds are being acquired or generated that will improve the accuracy and completion of this dataset. The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.

For the DOQQs the horizontal positional accuracy and the assurance of that accuracy depend, in part, on the accuracy of the data inputs to the rectification process. These inputs consist of the digital elevation model (DEM),aerotriangulation control and methods, the photo source camera calibration, scanner calibration, and aerial photographs that meet National Aerial Photography Program (NAPP) standards. The vertical accuracy of the verified USGS format DEM is equivalent to or better than a USGS level 1 or 2 DEM, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of no greater than 7.0 meters. Field control is acquired by third order class 1 or better survey methods sufficiently spaced to meet National Map Accuracy Standards (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale products. Aerial cameras have current certification from the USGS, National Mapping Division, Optical Science Laboratory. Test calibration scans are performed on all source photography scanners. Horizontal positional accuracy is determined by the Orthophoto Accuracy (ORACC) software program for DOQ data produced by the National Mapping Division. The program determines the accuracy by finding the line and sample coordinates of the passpoints in the DOQ and fitting these to their ground coordinates to develop a root mean square error (RMSE). From 4 to 9 points are checked. As a further accuracy test, the image line and sample coordinates of the DEM corners are transformed and compared with the actual X,Y DEM corner values to determine if they are within the RMSE. For the BLM GCDB Data the majority of coordinates in this dataset fall within +/- 40 feet spatial accuracy (the general rule of thumb to be called 1:24,000-scale data). For the DOQQs the horizontal positional accuracy and the assurance of that accuracy depend, in part, on the accuracy of the data inputs to the rectification process. These inputs consist of the digital elevation model (DEM),aerotriangulation control and methods, the photo source camera calibration, scanner calibration, and aerial photographs that meet National Aerial Photography Program (NAPP) standards. The vertical accuracy of the verified USGS format DEM is equivalent to or better than a USGS level 1 or 2 DEM, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of no greater than 7.0 meters. Field control is acquired by third order class 1 or better survey methods sufficiently spaced to meet National Map Accuracy Standards (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale products. Aerial cameras have current certification from the USGS, National Mapping Division, Optical Science Laboratory. Test calibration scans are performed on all source photography scanners. Horizontal positional accuracy is determined by the Orthophoto Accuracy (ORACC) software program for DOQ data produced by the National Mapping Division. The program determines the accuracy by finding the line and sample coordinates of the passpoints in the DOQ and fitting these to their ground coordinates to develop a root mean square error (RMSE). From 4 to 9 points are checked. As a further accuracy test, the image line and sample coordinates of the DEM corners are transformed and compared with the actual X,Y DEM corner values to determine if they are within the RMSE. Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. The native projection of the DWG is Hawaii State Plane Zone 2, NAD 83, US Foot. description.gco:CharacterString: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 12/17/2024 General, The park's “HAFE MONUMENTS – MASTER” access database was used to generate the Boundary Monuments ESRI Geodatabase Feature Class that much of the modifications in this Change Order are based on. Monument data was generated by using the “Add Data – XY Point Data” function in Arc Pro based on the WV State Plane N coordinate system. Monuments without XY data were omitted from this project. For all areas of the park, the HAFE tract and boundary data were shifted to align with the existing monument data maintained by the park and displayed in Arc Pro, except where noted otherwise. All shifts to the tract and boundary data represent the most current survey data available to, and stored at, the park.WV Tax Assessor data was consulted but generally not used for the modifications in this Change Order. Loudoun Heights (109-01,109-02, 105-02, 103-05, 103-06) Plats from the Hartmann Associates, Inc. survey of the Werner tracts from July 13, 2000 were georeferenced to the monument points to determine line curvature between points where necessary, but otherwise the boundary along Loudoun heights was snapped to the monument points. All plats were georeferenced using a first order polynomial transformation with a minimum of 3 control points. In the northern portion near the Potoma Wayside tract and boundary data were snapped to the most current existing monuments without the aid of georeferenced plats. There are multiple defunct monuments in this area that may have led to previous errors in the boundary. Monument metadata was consulted to determine the correct monuments to reference. NOTE: Hartmann Plat station point coordinates, when displayed as NAD 1983 State Plane West Virginia N FIPS 4701 (US Feet) are offset from the monument database data to the east. Unclear why this is or where the master monument DB coordinates, which appear to be correct, came from. Schoolhouse Ridge South (SHRS): (108-01, 108-03, 108-04, 108-05) A plat from the 1991 US Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) for the Sleepy Hollow Partnership and Marcus Enterprises tracts was used as a guide for determining the curvature of the boundary on the western side near the railroad tracks. However, due to the scale of the plat it was not possible to get an extremely accurate georeferenced image using a first order polynomial with 4 control points. Other transformations were not attempted. The 2002 plat “Survey of 60.00 Acres To Department of Treasury” indicates a discrepancy between HAFE’s exterior boundary monuments and the boundary depicted in the plat along the southern edge of the parcel, which is part of the transition of this parcel from NPS to Homeland Security. In this case the plat, aerial imagery, and official boundary agreed, and the boundary was maintained as-is rather than changed to fit the monuments. The remaining monuments agreed with the plat. The 2005 plat “Survey of Tract 108-01” was used to guide shifting the boundary to align with monuments in the northern portion of SHR-S. Schoolhouse Ridge North (SHRN) and Bolivar Heights: (102-33, 102-34). Plats that were georeferenced to determine the boundary for this area include: Plat of Survey Showing an Exemption Parcel and Residue (1987); Plat Showing a Boundary Line Adjustment The Property of the Civil War Preservation Trust (2002, Deed Book 961, Page 219); Survey of Tract 102-34 (2005); Plan and Profile for Construction of State Road Project No. F-64(6) Route No. U.S. 340 Sheets 19 and 30 (2007). These were used as a guide to make minor shifts to the boundary and tracts, primarily along US-340 and Bakerton Road, as well as around C.W. Shipley School. All of these were georeferenced using a 1st order polynomial transformation with 3-4 control points. Partial Survey HAFE Tract 102-33 (2009) did not align cleanly with boundary monuments and aerial imagery. Additional work will be needed to accurately define the boundary in this area. Nash Farm: (101-06, 102-03,102-05, 102-23, 102-24) The Plat for the Survey of Tracts 102-05, 102-23, 102-24 was used to make changes to the tracts and boundary data surrounding the Nash Farm. It was georeferenced using a 1st order polynomial transformation with 4 control points. The existing tract and boundary data did not consider the “paper street” on the northern boundary of the Nash Farm parcel (102-23) that belongs to the city of Harpers Ferry. Slight adjustments were also required along the southern edge of the property to correctly align with the plat and existing monument data. Union Street/Camp Hill: (103-41, 106-46, 106-06) The following plats were georeferenced to refine the boundary along Union Street: Survey of Tract 103-41 (1995); Survey of Tract 106-06 (2005); and Harpers Ferry National Historical Park, Jefferson County, West Virginia Dependent Survey (BLM 1997). The BLM survey was used to verify accuracy of monuments in this area and to tie in the other surveys. All of these were georeferenced using a 1st order polynomial transformation with 3-4 control points. The existing tracts and boundary data in this area appeared to correspond to older surveys, including the founding survey for the park, and did not consider the newer 1995 and 2005 surveys of the area. The boundary and tracts were adjusted slightly to align with the boundaries depicted in these newer surveys. Lower Town/CSX Boundary: (101-06, 106-07, 106-20, 106-32) The plat “CSX Transportation Property to be Conveyed to US Department of the Interior” was used to make slight adjustments to the park boundary and tracts located near the rail station and “The Point” in Lower Town. It was georeferenced using a 2nd order polynomial and 11 control points. Points were added along the north side of the CSX rail line corridor, plotted based on distance, direction, and curve data depicted on the file “1644.trv”. This survey file was originally generated by field survey based on existing monuments located along the rail line. The boundary was adjusted to follow these points. Potomac Wayside: (105-09) Boundary shifted to align with points taken on existing VDOT monuments located along the roadside. Points were taken with a Trimble R1 unit accurate to 1 meter. Attempted to georeference and extract data from the 1949 plat for Potomac Wayside but was not able to accurately georeference or decipher curve data that would have allowed for additional points and exact curvature to be used. Murphy Farm Area (103-43, 103-16, 103-17) There was a small extension at the southern end of Tract 103-43 that did not align with the boundary monument data or the georeferenced 2002 plat "Plat of Resurvey Showing Murphy Farm". We shifted the tract to align with the monument data, necessitating corresponding changes to the boundaries of adjacent tracts 103-16 and 103-17. Roman Catholic Diocese (106-08, 105-01, 106-26, 106-31) The tract lines for Tract 106-08 were slightly offset from the boundary monument data in this area. This is supported by the georeferenced 1993 plat "Survey of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Richmond, Virginia". We modified Tract 106-08's boundary to be snapped to the boundary monument data for this tract, necessitating corresponding changes to the boundaries of adjacent tracts 105-01, 106-26, and 106-31. UPDATE: 09/09/2021 Tract 103-46 status change from PRIV FEE to FED FEE. Update 09/03/2020: Park boundary revised to include Tract 108-07, which was added through a minor boundary revision. Notice of the revision is published at 83 Fed. Reg. 50,958 (October 10, 2018). Status of Tract 108-07 updated to FED in accordance with deed to the USA recorded in Jefferson Co., WV, in Book 1216, Page 149, on 12/10/2018. Tract 108-07 was plotted from deed referenced above.The linework for tracts 101-09 and 103-48 were updated in July 2016 using the document and survey named HAFE_101-09_103-48.pdf located here:http://landsnet.nps.gov/tractsnet/documents/HAFE/Miscellaneous/. Tract 106-07B was created using the document named HAFE106-07B which is located here: http://landsnet.nps.gov/tractsnet/documents/HAFE/Miscellaneous/. Tract 108-07 was created using Jefferson county WV parcel linework. North American Datum 1983 - West Virginia State Planes, US Foot projection grid. All tracts administered by HAFE were originally created from GIS data provided by the Natural Resource Division (NRD) in 2000. According to the NRD staff, the original dataset was cogo'd using ArcView. At this time, the curve function was not available, and the data is considered estimated. The GIS dataset was imported and is maintained in the Autodesk Land Desktop environment. All additional tracts and acquisitions since 2000 have been cogo from deeds, if a survey plat was not available. This data was georeferenced USGS DOQQ data. The Autodesk line work was created, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology was developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5 revised 2017. The entire unit was created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map were created. The tract and boundary data was then exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format and reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude by Lands Fort Collins Office. Since this data was created, edits have been made to the original ESRI Geodatabase Feature Class using Autodesk Civil 3D, ArcGIS Map, and ArcGIS Pro using appropriate local coordinate systems. This data is exported from these environments in either a ESRI Geodatabase Feature Class or geodatabase format using a North American Datum 1983 projection.

UPDATE: 06/12/2021 Inadvertently forgot to include Hawaii tax parcel number 393004002 in NPS tract 02-101. Copied parcel 393004002 from Hawaii Tax Map Feature Class http://hawaii.gov/dbedt/gis/tmk.htm), which was downloaded on 5/7/2008, and appended it to tract 02-101. UPDATE: 06/11/2021 Autodesk Land Desktop drawing was defined as HA - North American Datum 83, Hawaii State Plane, Zone I,US Foot. Downloaded Hawaii Tax Map Feature Class (http://hawaii.gov/dbedt/gis/tmk.htm) downloaded on 5/7/2008. It was determined that this layer was of outstanding quality, so it was used to georeference the tracts and boundary for this the drawing. description.gco:CharacterString: John Day Fossil Beds National Monument Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 07/08/2015 BLM GCDB data was used in completing the boundary for JODA. BLM GCDB line work was imported into the DWG and copied to the appropriate layer (either tract or boundary layer). The majority of tracts for the park were mapped using the GDBD data as well. For the USGS DLG Data Horizontal positional accuracy is based upon the use of USGS source quadrangles which are compiled to meet National Map Accuracy Standards (NMAS). NMAS horizontal accuracy requires that at least 90 percent of points tested are within 0.02 inches of the true position. The digital data are estimated to contain a horizontal positional error of less than or equal to 0.003 inches standard error in the two component directions relative to the source quadrangle. Comparison to the graphic source is used as control to assess digital positional accuracy. For the BLM GCDB Data the majority of coordinates in this dataset fall within +/- 40 feet spatial accuracy (the general rule of thumb to be called 1:24,000-scale data). For the DOQQs the horizontal positional accuracy and the assurance of that accuracy depend, in part, on the accuracy of the data inputs to the rectification process. These inputs consist of the digital elevation model (DEM),aerotriangulation control and methods, the photo source camera calibration, scanner calibration, and aerial photographs that meet National Aerial Photography Program (NAPP) standards. The vertical accuracy of the verified USGS format DEM is equivalent to or better than a USGS level 1 or 2 DEM, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of no greater than 7.0 meters. Field control is acquired by third order class 1 or better survey methods sufficiently spaced to meet National Map Accuracy Staandards (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale products. Aerial cameras have current certification from the USGS, National Mapping Division, Optical Science Laboratory. Test calibration scans are performed on all source photography scanners. Horizontal positional accuracy is determined by the Orthophoto Accuracy (ORACC) software program for DOQ data produced by the National Mapping Division. The program determines the accuracy by finding the line and sample coordinates of the passpoints in the DOQ and fitting these to their ground coordinates to develop a root mean square error (RMSE). From 4 to 9 points are checked. As a further accuracy test, the image line and sample coordinates of the DEM corners are transformed and compared with the actual X,Y DEM corner values to determine if they are within the RMSE. Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. The native coordinate system for the DWG was Oregon State Plane Zone North, NAD83. The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.

description.gco:CharacterString: John F. Kennedy Birthplace National Historical Site Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 11/01/2010 The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step. Individual Parcel data was obtained from the MassGIS (MASSACHUSETTS GIS Department). The parcel data set was clipped to the Township of Brookline. The line work was then copied to the appropriate layer in order to complete the mapping of the boundary and overlayed with NAIP DOQQ from 2009. The Level II digital parcel data were provided to MassGIS by communities, or their regional planning agency partners, that received parcel grants from MassGIS in 2002 and 2006. Each municipality's parcels found in this data set were provided to MassGIS separately and then appended together to form this single data layer. Most of the parcel data included in this data layer has not been updated since it was received by MassGIS in 2002/2003 and 2006. The grant recipients were required to deliver digital parcel data complying with "Level II" of the MassGIS Standard for Digital Parcels and Related Data Sets. The data submitted by grant recipients were subjected to a rigorous quality assurance process to ensure compliance with the standard. The standard establishes requirements for how parcel boundaries are compiled. It also requires establishing a few attributes of the polygons that are unique to the standard. In addition, the standard requires that a minimum selection of information from the assessor's database be included in a separate database table that can be linked to the parcel polygons. At Level II of the standard, an "intersection table" is required, which makes it possible to correctly model the one-to-many and many-to-many relationships that exist between assessor map polygons and assessor databases. Coordinate system used was State Plane Zone MA Mainland for the city of Brookline. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. The positional accuracy of this dataset is dependent upon the scales of the maps which this dataset is drawn from. Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy.

description.gco:CharacterString: Katmai National Park and Preserve Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 03/01/2009 In September 1993, the KATM hand-drawn mylar Land Resources Division segment sheets were created. They were continually revised as needed until 2001. In 1996, the park boundary and tracts were digitized from the Katmai National Park and Preserve segment maps by NPS-contractor GeoNorth Inc. using ESRI software in the form of coverages, and, under the direction of the GIS and Lands Teams. Other digital sources used in the initial digital data set included: best available hydrography and digital public lands survey system maps. In 1997, all disposed tracts outside of the park boundary were dropped from the GIS. From 1999 to 2001, Encompass Mapping and Data, under contract to NPS and using ESRI software in the form of coverages, began a major update and revision process of the park boundary and tracts. Attribute and linework errors were resolved, better digital sources were used (DOQQs, survey data, revised USGS hydrography, PLSS, etc.), and land status changes were updated. From 2002 to 2009, many boundary and tract changes were either performed by the cartographer for the Alaska Land Resources Program Center using either Autodesk or ArcGIS software, then submitted in the form of Autodesk-exported or native ArcGIS shapefiles, jpegs, and requested attribute changes to Encompass Mapping and Data; or, the data was created/edited by Encompass Mapping and Data under the direction of the Lands cartographer. Most of the changes made by the Lands cartographer consisted of moving tracts to more accurate locations, modifying native corporations/allotments, cogoing the U.S., M.S., BLM, and NPS surveys using survey and Autodesk software, using the written legal descriptions for the park boundaries, using private and federal deed descriptions/plats, and using better orthophoto/DRG data to digitize shorelines, ridge boundaries, etc. In 2007, the islands and small portions of the coastline were redefined using satellite imagery. However, the bulk of the Mean High Water (MHW) shoreline for KATM is approximate and needs a better shoreline if and when better satellite ortho-imagery becomes available. Encompass converted the data into ArcInfo files, attributed it, and submitted the data each time to the GIS team for inclusion into the GIS Permanent Data Set (PDS). NPS administrative parcels outside of the park were mapped by Lands during 2007-2008. In 2008, the Cobell restrictions on gov't. use of Native Allotment data were lifted so all Native Allotment data were returned to the GIS/Lands geodatabase. During 2009, the common boundary with the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service- Becharof Refuge and the KATM boundary was edited and agreed upon. This was accomplished by the Alaska Lands cartographer and GIS specialists from both agencies. In April 2009, Encompass Mapping and Data converted all lands data from coverages into a land status and boundary geodatabase created under contract to the AKRO-GIS Team. Specifications as delineated by GIS and Lands personnel were followed. In progress 2009, many of the native allotments are being cogoed-in by Lands cartographers. During 2008+, BLM-produced digital cogoed native allotments and other U.S. Surveys are also being incorporated into the NPS lands system after comparing to NPS cogo work or other maps. Tract and boundary data is continually updated with land status changes and ongoing improvement of linework/attribution as better source information becomes available. The tract and boundary data has all been reprojected (when needed) to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude. State tracts were created for the following navigable waters: Alagnak River, Nonvianuk River, Kukaklek Lake, and Nonvianuk Lake. The 2000 Alagnak River Corridor Photo Mosaic was used for the bulk of the shoreline digitizing. A Riparian Specialist with the BLM were consulted for mapping the tract shoreline at the estimated Ordinary High Water Mark (OHWM). A major remapping effort was completed for ~90% of the native allotments and other small private parcels. They were systematically revised and/or checked for correct location and conveyance status. Most were remapped by COGOing in US Survey plats and/or legal descriptions or using BLM-COGOed data. Previous to these edits, most small tracts were digitized from the hard copy Segment Sheets.In addition, satellite and aerial photo ortho imagery were used to move the tracts to better locations when the latitude/longitude of the parcels were too approximate or unknown. New tracts have been broken out of existing tracts where a subdivision and sale has been made to a non-native person(s). Continuous minor editing has been performed on park boundaries where better orthoimagery and/or common boundary agreements with adjoining federal agencies have been agreed upon per the "Alaska Common Boundary Initiative". No acreage changes are taking place. Native corporation conveyance actions have been updated as the changes take place. This involves deleting selections in some cases to changing from selected status into conveyed status. Survey plats and notes are always used to COGO in the boundaries. All tracts outside the park boundaries have now been mapped.

description.gco:CharacterString: Keweenaw Mountain National Battlefield Park Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE: 09/22/2025 Converted CAD dataset to GDB using script provided by WASO. Projected and converted CAD dataset provided by surveyor for inclusion in the tract and boundaries dataset to create tract 01-142. UPDATE: 09/23/2020 See Anthony Marshall for detail on this update. POC: Xiaodong Hong, Manager, Geographic Information Systems, (703) 671-1900. Email: xhong@avineon.com. Digitized line work was then verified by the SER Office personnel from deeds, legal descriptions, and survey data (when available). Map Projection is Georgia State Plane, NAD27, US foot . When discrepancies were identified, individual tracts were re-plotted by use of COGO, using AutoCAD LDD. Data was geo-referenced to DOQQ, Georgia State Plane, NAD 83. Topology was created for park boundary and individual tracts. Primary validation of cartographic attributes was verified by displaying the lines in both database and the spatial coverage, but no formal tests were performed. Database attributes were linked during the topology creation process. Database attributes were retrieved from the National Park Service, Management Information System, Master Deeds List (MIS/MDL). Clean Topology was developed and attributes were assigned in AutoCad Map using the Drawing Clean-up function at a tolerance level of 0.10 and Object Data links. The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.
