description.gco:CharacterString: White Sands National Monument UPDATE 03/14/2023 Tract 01-193 removed from boundary. There is some confusion about the status of this tract (inside vs outside boundary) and most likely originates from the historical boundary changes related to US-70 ROW. In 1938, specific legislation was enacted (PP 2295, 53 Stat. 2465) that removed any lands required for US-70 ROW from the boundary (this tract was outside the boundary at that time), however the 1942 PL 77-539, 56 Stat. 326 appears to include this tract within boundary. This tract is currently being used and maintained by the State of New Mexico for US-70, and NPS has no interest in retaining this tract for park purposes. Status of this tract needs to be verified, but as of now it has been removed from boundary to coincide with the internal database. Most boundary and tract line work was derived and georeferenced from CadNSDI data imported into AutoCAD Civil 3D. Tracts bisected by US-70 were derived from Highway ROW survey plan sets. This update is provided to depict the tract and boundary modifications resulting from the 2020 National Defense Authorization Act (Dec. 20, 2019) transfer of lands between NPS and Dept. of the Army (White Sands Missile Range). The source coordinate system used in AutoCAD Civil 3D is North American Datum 1983, New Mexico State Plane, Central Zone, US Survey Foot. The AutoCAD line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures (LAPS) Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from AutoCAD to a shape file format in a single step.

description.gco:CharacterString: Wind Cave National Park Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE 06/11/2025 Restore park boundary around 01-167. This issue was not resolved in the last quarterly update. UPDATE 01/31/2025 Update restored the park boundary around Tract 01-167 UPDATE 04/19/2016 BLM GDBC digital flat files were downloaded on 04/12/2010 for the area that encompasses WICA. This line work was used to create all aliquot part tracts as shown on segment map 01. This segment map was imported into AutoDesk and matched to PLSS linework. T5S R6E Sections 8, 9, 11, 14, 16, 21, 22, 23, 26, 27, and 34. The ROW for county roads 65 and 66 was created by onscreen digitizing the centerline of the roadway utilizing 2008 NAIP 1m imagery. This centerline was offset 33 feet on either side to produce a 66 feet wide right of way as described in deed 49. This right of way includes tracts 01-142 and 01-119. Deed 46, which describes tract 01-142 states that the ROW exits the park in Section 8 and re-enters in section 6 of T5n R6E. This deed was written in 1953, and the roadway was altered so that it does not exit the park in section 8, as seen in the proposed 1951 Road and Trail System Plan map for WICA (NP-WC-2023-B). Taking the road alteration into consideration, the right of way for tract 01-142 was ended where the roadway appeared to exit the park before the alteration as seen in 2008 NAIP 1m aerial imagery. Deed 49 provides bearing and distance measurements for tract 01-119 as stated in the original deed issued in 1926. When drawn utilizing the cogo commands in AutoDesk and transformed around known points, the tract boundaries are still significantly different from the actual roadway as seen in 2008 NAIP 1m aerial imagery. Since this same imagery was used to portray all other roadways, it was determined to on screen digitize the centerline of this portion of county road 65, offset the centerline 33 feet on either side, and use the bearing and distance measurements provided in deed 49 to determine the northernmost boundary for tract 01-119 which lies in the NE 1/4 NE1/4 of section 27, T5S R6E. The right of way for the Custer County Road in T5s R5E sections 11, and 14 was created by onscreen digitizing the centerline of the roadway utilizing 2008 NAIP 1m imagery. The centerline was offset 33 feet on either side to produce a 66 feet wide right of way. The majority of the boundaries for tracts 01-106, 01-133, and 01-103 were detailed in the GCDB linework. Short segments that were not included in the GCDB linework were drawn by snapping to existing GCDB linework. Tracts 01-147, 01-154, 01-155, 01-156, and 01-157 found in T5S R5E sections 27, 28, 32, 33, and 34, representing a water supply pipeline right of way for WICA, were drawn using cogo commands in AutoDesk based on distance and bearing measurements from the 1931 survey map NP-WC-4933. Tracts 01-147, 01-155, and 01-157 are described in deed 5 (dated August 28, 1931), but distance and bearings from deed 5 vary from those documented in survey map NP-WC-4933 (Approved October 16, 1931), and so the survey map was used for the entire portion of the pipeline. Once drawn, the pipeline was transformed around two known points (a point NW 20d09' 732.8 feet from the Southwest corner of the southeast quarter of section 28 as shown on survey map NP-WC-4933, and a point on the section boundary line of sections 26 and 27 of T5S R5E (also the park boundary) 82 feet north of the southern line of the above mentioned sections as described in deed 5 as the ending place of the right-of-way). The right-of-way distance for this pipeline was not described in any available documentation. Therefore, the right-of-way was drawn at 5 feet which, when calculated in AutoCAD, resulted in acreage measurements that most closely resembled the acreage listed for each tract in their original deeds. Tract 01-149 found in T5S R5E section 28 was drawn using cogo commands in AutoCAD based on survey map 108/80025 dated February 1990. The distance and direction from this survey vary slightly from the survey utilized to describe this tract in deed 5 dated August 21, 1931. The basis of bearing for the 1990 survey was the north-south section line between sections 27 and 28 which had a bearing of 0deg 07' 20". The current GCDB bearing for this same line is 2deg 07' 11.06". This difference was accounted for by rotating the cogo'ed linework -1deg59'.06". Tracts 01-158, 01-159, 01-160, 01-161, 01-162, 01-163, and 01-164 located in T6S R5E section 23 and 24 were drawn based on the legal descriptions for their respective deeds (deeds: 57 - 61). The western boundary of tract 02-102 located in section 24 T6S5E and section 30 T6S6E was drawn in accordance with survey Affidavits recorded in Misc. Book 40 pages 891, 892, 896, 899, and 396. Each survey was drawn using cogo commands in AutoCAD. The resulting linework was then transformed around points x=1139075.0058, y=445870.851 and x=1137762.2605, y=445919.1208 to match the most recent GCDB linework. Lots 53 and 54 of the Battle Mountain Subdivision were cogo'ed based on Survey Affidavit recorded in Misc. Book 12, page 284 and transformed around points x=1136449.5071, y=445967.3899 and x=1136515.0635, y=447297.0151 to match GCDB linework. The southern boundary of tract 02-102 following the County Road 101 33 foot right of way in section 30, T6S6E was cogo'ed based on Survey Affidavits recorded in Misc. Book 40, pages 894, 895, 896, 897, 898, and 900. Each survey was drawn using cogo commands in AutoCAD. The resulting linework was then transformed around points x=1140108.9058, y=441857.7291 and x=1141427.5952, y=441809.3942 to match GCDB linework. The County Road 101 33 foot right of way in section 20, T6N6E was cogo'ed based on Survey Affidavit recorded in Misc. Book 40, page 893. The survey was drawn using cogo commands in AutoCAD and the resulting linework was rotated -2d41'.07" around point x=1144175.3087, y=444353.8990 to match GCDB linework. The southern boundary for the park in T6s R5E Section 24 follows the east side of a 50 foot right-of-way for Highway 385 per survey map wc 108/80026, 1993. The right of way was drawn at 50 feet according to survey map np:wc 2034, 1956. Tracts 01-170 and 01-171 were drawn from Deed 63. Tracts 01-172 was cogo'd from a Warranty Deed dated August 20, 2015 and Tract 01-173 from a Warranty Deed dated May 26, 2015, filed in Custer County, South Dakota. NAD83 South Dakota State Planes, South Zone, US Foot was used as the source coordinate system for the Autodesk Land Desktop project. description.gco:CharacterString: Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE 03/31/2022 In Nov. 1992, the WRST hand-drawn mylar Land Resources Division segment sheets 01-42 were created by the Alaska Regional Office Lands cartographer. They were continually revised as needed until 2003. In 1996, the park boundary and tracts were digitized from the Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve segment maps by NPS-contractor GeoNorth Inc. using ESRI software in the form of coverages, and, under the direction of the GIS and Lands Teams. Other digital sources used in the initial digital data set included: best available hydrography and digital public lands survey system maps. In 1997, all disposed tracts outside the park boundary were dropped from the GIS. From 1999 to 2001, Encompass Mapping and Data, under contract to NPS and using ESRI software in the form of coverages, began a major update and revision process of the park boundary and tracts. Attribute and linework errors were resolved, better digital sources were used (DOQQs, survey data, revised USGS hydrography, PLSS, etc.), and land status changes were updated. From 2002 to 2009, many boundary and tract changes were either performed by the cartographer for the Alaska Land Resources Program Center using either Autodesk or ArcGIS software, then submitted in the form of Autodesk-exported or native ArcGIS shapefiles, jpegs, and requested attribute changes to Encompass Mapping and Data; or, the data was created/edited by Encompass Mapping and Data under the direction of the Lands cartographer. Most of the changes made by the Lands cartographer consisted of moving tracts to more accurate locations, modifying native corporations/allotments, cogoing the U.S., M.S., BLM, and NPS surveys using survey and Autodesk software, using the written legal descriptions for the park boundaries, using private and federal deed descriptions/plats, and using better orthophoto/DRG data to digitize shorelines, ridge boundaries, etc. Encompass converted the data into ArcInfo files, attributed it, and submitted the data each time to the GIS team for inclusion into the GIS Permanent Data Set (PDS). The marine shoreline needs to be remapped when/if better MHW shoreline data becomes available (portions of Icy Bay shoreline and glacier edges were remapped from . From 1982 to 2009, most of the patented mining claims and many of the other private tracts have been either surveyed by the NPS/BLM or tract corners have been located using resource-grade GPS mostly by the NPS-WRST-Park Geologist and some by NPS-AKRO-Mining & Minerals personnel. WRST has probably received the most attention to better locating inholdings to their correct location (most of the older surveys have inaccurate beginning lat/long locations). Newer private survey data for McCarthy from Kean & Assoc., Kennicott survey data from newer BLM surveys, and recent State of Alaska DOT roadway maps/survey plats/GPS road centerline data/ROW's have all been used to refine the lands data from 2002 to 2009. From 2008 to 2009, the Tetlin Wildlife Refuge and WRST park boundary were compared and minorly adjusted to come up with one commonly agreed boundary. Plans are underway to come to agreement with the Forest Service on the common boundaries near the Alsek River and Bremner/Copper River areas during 2009+. During 2006-08, Lands cogoed in most of the remaining native allotments/private tracts using park GPS data and the U.S. Survey plats. During 2008+, BLM-produced digital cogoed native allotments and other U.S. Surveys are also being incorporated into the NPS lands system after comparing to NPS cogo work or other maps. Also during 2008, the Cobell restrictions on use of Native Allotment data were lifted so all Native Allotment data were returned to the GIS/Lands geodatabase. In April 2009, Encompass Mapping and Data converted all lands data from coverages into a land status and boundary geodatabase created under contract to the AKRO-GIS Team. Specifications as delineated by GIS and Lands personnel were followed. Also in 2009, the selected native corporation lands were reduced because they had overselected the amount of lands they will actually be able to receive under ANCSA regulations. Hence, the regional and village corporations "prioritized" their selections- most of these lands will likely go to patent during 2009+. Tract and boundary data are continually updated with land status changes and ongoing improvement of linework/attribution as better source information becomes available. The tract and boundary data has all been reprojected (when needed) to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude and longitude. A major remapping effort was completed for ~90% of the native allotments and other small private parcels. They were systematically revised and/or checked for correct location and conveyance status. Most were remapped by COGOing in US Survey plats and/or legal descriptions or using BLM-COGOed data. Previous to these edits, most small tracts were digitized from the hard copy Segment Sheets.In addition, satellite and aerial photo ortho imagery were used to move the tracts to better locations when the latitude/longitude of the parcels were too approximate or unknown. New tracts have been broken out of existing tracts where a subdivision and sale has been made to a non-native person(s). Continuous minor editing has been performed on park boundaries where better orthoimagery and/or common boundary agreements with adjoining federal agencies have been agreed upon per the "Alaska Common Boundary Initiative". No acreage changes are taking place. Native corporation conveyance actions have been updated as the changes take place. This involves deleting selections in some cases to changing from selected status into conveyed status. Survey plats and notes are always used to COGO in the boundaries. All tracts outside the park boundaries have now been mapped.

description.gco:CharacterString: Wright Brothers National Memorial Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE 05/24/2011 Dare county parcel data was obtained for Dare county GIS. The native projection for the parcel data was NAD 27. The parce line work was reprojected to NAD 83 in order to ensure no geographic shifting. The tracts and boundary for WRBR were copied from Dare County assessor's parcel data. They were then copied to their appropriate layer; either the tract layer or boundary layer. Any remaining tracts were then COGO'd from deeds. The line work was laid over NAIP aerial imagery for the area as well.For the DOQQs the horizontal positional accuracy and the assurance of that accuracy depend, in part, on the accuracy of the data inputs to the rectification process. These inputs consist of the digital elevation model (DEM),aerotriangulation control and methods, the photo source camera calibration, scanner calibration, and aerial photographs that meet National Aerial Photography Program (NAPP) standards. The vertical accuracy of the verified USGS format DEM is equivalent to or better than a USGS level 1 or 2 DEM, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of no greater than 7.0 meters. Field control is acquired by third order class 1 or better survey methods sufficiently spaced to meet National Map Accuracy Staandards (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale products. Aerial cameras have current certification from the USGS, National Mapping Division, Optical Science Laboratory. Test calibration scans are performed on all source photography scanners. Horizontal positional accuracy is determined by the Orthophoto Accuracy (ORACC) software program for DOQ data produced by the National Mapping Division. The program determines the accuracy by finding the line and sample coordinates of the passpoints in the DOQ and fitting these to their ground coordinates to develop a root mean square error (RMSE). From 4 to 9 points are checked. As a further accuracy test, the image line and sample coordinates of the DEM corners are transformed and compared with the actual X,Y DEM corner values to determine if they are within the RMSE. For the BLM GCDB Data the majority of coordinates in this dataset fall within +/- 40 feet spatial accuracy (the general rule of thumb to be called 1:24,000-scale data). For the DOQQs the horizontal positional accuracy and the assurance of that accuracy depend, in part, on the accuracy of the data inputs to the rectification process. These inputs consist of the digital elevation model (DEM),aerotriangulation control and methods, the photo source camera calibration, scanner calibration, and aerial photographs that meet National Aerial Photography Program (NAPP) standards. The vertical accuracy of the verified USGS format DEM is equivalent to or better than a USGS level 1 or 2 DEM, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of no greater than 7.0 meters. Field control is acquired by third order class 1 or better survey methods sufficiently spaced to meet National Map Accuracy Staandards (NMAS) for 1:12,000-scale products. Aerial cameras have current certification from the USGS, National Mapping Division, Optical Science Laboratory. Test calibration scans are performed on all source photography scanners. Horizontal positional accuracy is determined by the Orthophoto Accuracy (ORACC) software program for DOQ data produced by the National Mapping Division. The program determines the accuracy by finding the line and sample coordinates of the passpoints in the DOQ and fitting these to their ground coordinates to develop a root mean square error (RMSE). From 4 to 9 points are checked. As a further accuracy test, the image line and sample coordinates of the DEM corners are transformed and compared with the actual X,Y DEM corner values to determine if they are within the RMSE. Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. The native projection of the DWG was NC State Plane, NAD 83, US Foot. The Autodesk line work is imported, edited, attributed, approved, and a link and node topology is developed both for the tract and boundary data layers according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a geographically contiguous model space and separate layouts representing each individual segment map are created. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported from Autodesk to an ArcView shape file format in a single step.

description.gco:CharacterString: Yukon-Charley Rivers National Preserve Tract and Boundary Data UPDATE 03/21/2019 In March 1994, the YUCH hand-drawn mylar Land Resources Division segment sheets 01-05 were created by the Alaska Regional Office Lands cartographer. They were continually revised as needed until 2002. In 1996, the park boundary and tracts were digitized from the Yukon-Charley National Preserve segment maps by NPS-contractor GeoNorth Inc. using ESRI software in the form of coverages, and, under the direction of the GIS and Lands Teams. Other digital sources used in the initial digital data set included: best available hydrography and digital public lands survey system maps. In 1997, all disposed tracts outside the park boundary were dropped from the GIS. From 1999 to 2001, Encompass Mapping and Data, under contract to NPS and using ESRI software in the form of coverages, began a major update and revision process of the park boundary and tracts. Attribute and linework errors were resolved, better digital sources were used (DOQQs, survey data, revised USGS hydrography, PLSS, etc.), and land status changes were updated. From 2002 to 2009, many boundary and tract changes were either performed by the cartographer for the Alaska Land Resources Program Center using either Autodesk or ArcGIS software, then submitted in the form of Autodesk-exported or native ArcGIS shapefiles, jpegs, and requested attribute changes to Encompass Mapping and Data; or, the data was created/edited by Encompass Mapping and Data under the direction of the Lands cartographer. Most of the changes made by the Lands cartographer consisted of moving tracts to more accurate locations, modifying native corporations/allotments, cogoing the U.S., M.S., BLM, and NPS surveys using survey and Autodesk software, using the written legal descriptions for the park boundaries, using private and federal deed descriptions/plats, and using better orthophoto/DRG data to digitize shorelines, ridge boundaries, etc. Encompass converted the data into ArcInfo files, attributed it, and submitted the data each time to the GIS team for inclusion into the GIS Permanent Data Set (PDS). NPS administrative parcels outside of the park were mapped by Lands during 2007-2008. Also during 2007-2008, Lands cogoed in some of the native allotments from the U.S. Surveys and incorporated them into the NPS lands system. During 2008+, BLM-produced digital cogoed native allotments and other U.S. Surveys are also being incorporated into the NPS lands system after comparing to NPS cogo work or other maps. Also during 2008, the Cobell restrictions on use of Native Allotment data were lifted so all Native Allotment data were returned to the GIS/Lands geodatabase. In April 2009, Encompass Mapping and Data converted all lands data from coverages into a land status and boundary geodatabase created under contract to the AKRO-GIS Team. Specifications as delineated by GIS and Lands personnel were followed. Also in 2009, the selected native corporation lands were reduced because they had overselected the amount of lands they will actually be able to receive under ANCSA regulations. Hence, the regional and village corporations "prioritized" their selections- most of these lands will likely go to patent during 2009+ (some of the prioritized selected lands in YUCH were recently IC'd or patented in 2008). Tract and boundary data are continually updated with land status changes and ongoing improvement of linework/attribution as better source information becomes available. The tract and boundary data has all been reprojected (when needed) to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude and longitude. A major remapping effort was completed for ~90% of the native allotments and other small private parcels. They were systematically revised and/or checked for correct location and conveyance status. Most were remapped by COGOing in US Survey plats and/or legal descriptions or using BLM-COGOed data. Previous to these edits, most small tracts were digitized from the hard copy Segment Sheets. In addition, satellite and aerial photo ortho imagery were used to move the tracts to better locations when the latitude/longitude of the parcels were too approximate or unknown. New tracts have been broken out of existing tracts where a subdivision and sale has been made to a non-native person(s). Continuous minor editing has been performed on park boundaries where better orthoimagery and/or common boundary agreements with adjoining federal agencies have been agreed upon per the "Alaska Common Boundary Initiative". No acreage changes are taking place. Native corporation conveyance actions have been updated as the changes take place. This involves deleting selections in some cases to changing from selected status into conveyed status. Survey plats and notes are always used to COGO in the boundaries. All tracts outside the park boundaries have now been mapped.

measureDescription.gco:CharacterString: The data set is complete but subject to continual updates to reflect boundary amendments, legislation, and acquisitions, improved source material, and better processing techniques. The data is being regularly updated with verified boundaries from NPS Land Resources Program. Boundaries with the word "Lands" starting the GIS_NOTES attribute have completed the Land Resources Program entire QA/QC processes. Boundaries that begin with the word "Preliminary" in the GIS_NOTES field, while generally created using the same methods as the "Lands" boundaries, have not completed the entire QA/QC process as should be treated as preliminary data only. The boundary polygons represent the current legislated boundary of a given NPS unit. NPS does not necessarily have full fee ownership or hold another interest (easement, right of way, etc...) in all parcels contained within this boundary. Equivalently NPS may own or have an interest in parcels outside the legislated boundary of a given unit. In order to obtain complete information about current NPS interests both inside and outside the units legislated boundary, the tract files and/or fee boundary file provided by the Land Resources Program should be used in conjunction with this boundary data. Please contact the data originator with any coments, questions, or update suggestions.

description.gco:CharacterString: NPS Director's Order ?Inv=True#25 states: "Land status maps will be prepared to identify the ownership of the lands within the authorized boundaries of the park unit. These maps, showing ownership and acreage, are the 'official record' of the acreage of Federal and non-federal lands within the park boundaries. While these maps are the official record of the lands and acreage within the unit's authorized boundaries, they are not of survey quality and not intended to be used for survey purposes." As such this data is intended for use as a tool for GIS analysis. It is in no way intended for engineering or legal purposes. The data accuracy is checked against best available sources which may be dated and vary by location. NPS assumes no liability for use of this data. Boundary polygons have been created by the Lands Resources Program according to the procedures defined in the Lands Acquisition Procedures Manual. Boundaries were created with data provided by Parks, Region, and Program offices. This data includes but is not limited to deeds, legal descriptions, legislation, survey plats, change orders, segment maps, and the ownership databases of the Land Resources Program. The supporting documentation used to create this data is available in the document archives on LandsNet. (http://landsnet.nps.gov) and in Lands regional offices. Users are strongly encouraged to contact their regional Lands office with questions, comments or for additional information. Map features from all sources have been adjusted to achieve a ‘best fit’ registration to the ownership parcels. While great care was taken in this process, maps from different sources rarely agree as to the precise location of geographic features. The relative positioning of map features to one another results from combining different map sources without field ‘ground truthing’. Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. This data is in a status of continual update, and as newer/better data becomes available, it will be included in this boundary dataset. Any person or entity that relies on this data, does so at their own risk. This data is updated quarterly.
